units.text: Begin with the request on the left. AWS WAF can inspect request components such as the URI path, headers, query string, and body, subject to the resource's inspection limits.
Follow the arrow into the web ACL. Managed rule groups, custom rules, rate-based rules, and bot controls help decide which requests reach the protected application.
Read the lower panels in order. Allow and Block terminate rule evaluation, while Count continues it. If no terminating rule decides the request, the web ACL default action applies.

With the full slide visible, start new protections in Count, inspect sampled requests and logs, and tune false positives before enforcement. WAF complements network controls rather than replacing them.

Start on the left, where legitimate users and unwanted traffic approach the application perimeter. Shield Standard supplies automatic baseline protection against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks.
Move across the edge-services panel. CloudFront, Route fifty-three, and Global Accelerator serve different purposes; choose the appropriate service for resilient exposure of your workload.
The right-hand panels combine application request filtering with a resilient application across Availability Zones. Restrict origin access so attackers cannot bypass the intended edge controls.
The full slide combines several layers. Shield Advanced adds subscription-based capabilities for eligible resources, while monitoring, incident response, and capacity planning remain necessary.
